prep.what: Add M3 vision-based detection to the label lane v2, enabling AI-powered label identification during takeoff.
prep.understand: The label lane v2 is part of the 95% Engine Upgrade. M3 refers to the third model integration milestone. Need to understand current label detection pipeline and where M3 hooks in.
approach: Review existing label lane v1 implementation and diff with v2 spec
Identify integration points for M3 vision model in the detection pipeline
Implement vision model call with proper error handling and fallback to rule-based detection
Write unit tests for the new lane logic
resources: M3 model API docs / existing M3 integration in other lanes

prep.what: Implement a durable job queue for the Tasks Platform so sweeper and CI jobs survive process restarts.
prep.understand: The current system likely runs jobs in-process. A durable queue persists job state so that if the daemon crashes, jobs resume on restart. This is a foundational piece for M3 Phase 6 CI/deploy.
approach: Define the job queue schema (job_id, type, payload, status, retries, created_at, updated_at)
Choose persistence layer (SQLite or append-only file) and implement enqueue/dequeue/ack
Wire the sweeper and CI triggers to enqueue rather than call directly
Add retry logic with exponential backoff and dead-letter handling
Write integration test for crash-recovery scenario
resources: Existing sweeper code in claude-todos-skill repo
SQLite docs for WAL mode (for concurrent reader/writer safety)

prep.what: Add a docker-based integration test that validates the writer component works correctly inside the container environment.
prep.understand: The writer is likely the component that pushes task updates back to repos. Docker integration tests catch issues that unit tests miss (file permissions, network, env vars).
approach: Identify the writer's entry point and key behaviors to test
Write a docker-compose or test script that spins up the writer container with a mock repo
Assert correct write behavior, error handling, and cleanup
resources: Existing docker test patterns in the repo (if any)

prep.what: Continue in-progress work to associate assembly sets with individual rooms in the takeoff output, enabling per-room material lists.
prep.understand: Currently assemblies are project-level aggregates. This task breaks them down per room so contractors can pull materials for each room individually. Already in progress — need to pick up from current state.
approach: Review in-progress branch / last commit to understand current state
Complete room-to-assembly mapping data structure
Update aggregation logic to group assembly items by room_id
Update API/output schema to include per_room_assemblies field
Test with a sample takeoff that has multi-room data
resources: In-progress branch for t18 in takeoff-engine repo

prep.what: Add a cross-process lock to the daemon so that concurrent refresh operations don't corrupt state when multiple daemon instances run.
prep.understand: Without a lock, two daemon processes refreshing simultaneously can create race conditions on shared files or DB state. Need a file lock or DB-level lock that is safe across processes.
approach: Identify where refresh is triggered in the daemon code
Implement a file-based lock (fcntl.flock) or SQLite advisory lock around the refresh critical section
Add timeout and stale-lock detection to prevent deadlocks
Write a test that spawns two daemon processes and verifies only one refresh runs at a time
resources: Python fcntl or filelock library docs

prep.what: Replace floating Docker image tags in the sandbox CI config with pinned SHA digests to ensure reproducible builds.
prep.understand: Using :latest or semver tags means the sandbox image can change silently. Digest pinning guarantees the exact same image bytes every run.
approach: Find all Docker image references in sandbox Dockerfiles / CI configs
Pull each image and capture its SHA256 digest (docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
Replace tags with @sha256:... references
Verify CI still passes with pinned digests
resources: Sandbox Dockerfile and CI workflow files in claude-todos-skill repo
Docker Hub or ghcr.io for current digest lookup
